entries.name: partial information decomposition
entries.senseHere: A method that splits what several input neurons tell you about a target neuron into overlapping, unique, and combined-only parts. It lets researchers separate simple passing-on of signals from real processing.

entries.name: rich club
entries.senseHere: A small set of the best-connected neurons that are tightly linked to each other, and that together carry most of the information flow in the network.

entries.name: multielectrode array
entries.background: A flat grid of many tiny electrodes that records electrical activity from many neurons at once.

entries.name: mutual information
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much knowing one neuron's activity lets you guess another's. It is symmetric and has no direction, so it does not show flow from one neuron to another.

entries.name: transfer entropy
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much one neuron's past helps predict another neuron's next state, beyond what that neuron's own past already predicts. It gives a direction to the flow of information.

entries.name: effective network
entries.senseHere: A map of which neurons seem to influence which others, built from statistical analysis of their activity rather than from anatomy.

entries.name: partial information atoms
entries.senseHere: The smallest non-overlapping pieces into which the total information from inputs about a target is divided. Each piece is a distinct way the inputs share information.

entries.name: synergy
entries.senseHere: Information about a target neuron that appears only when you look at several input neurons together, and not from any single one. The article treats it as a measure of computation.

entries.name: redundancy
entries.senseHere: Information about the target neuron that several input neurons each carry separately, so the same information is counted more than once.

entries.name: unique information
entries.senseHere: Information about the target neuron that only one particular input neuron provides, and the other inputs do not.

entries.name: Williams and Beer
entries.background: Paul Williams and Randall Beer, researchers who in 2010 introduced partial information decomposition. Their original redundancy formula is called Imin.

entries.name: redundancy function
entries.senseHere: A formula that fixes how much information counts as shared by several inputs. No single formula is agreed on, and the choice changes the results, so each one has trade-offs.

entries.name: computational triad
entries.senseHere: A group of three neurons in which two source neurons both connect to one shared target neuron. It is the basic unit the authors analyze.

entries.name: partial information lattice
entries.senseHere: A layered diagram that arranges every possible way a group of input neurons can share information about a target. Each point on it is one separate piece of information.

entries.name: organotypic cultures
entries.background: Thin slices of brain tissue kept alive in nutrient fluid in a dish. They regrow connections resembling those in an intact brain.

entries.name: Discrete Information Theory toolbox
entries.background: A Python software package for information-theoretic calculations on discrete variables. It includes many redundancy functions.

entries.name: IDTxl
entries.background: A Python software package for information-theoretic analysis of time series, including transfer entropy.

entries.name: Dedekind number
entries.background: A sequence of integers that counts certain collections of subsets. It grows extremely fast, and only a few terms are known.

entries.name: O-information
entries.senseHere: A single-number summary of whether a group of neurons is dominated by redundancy or synergy. It is easier to compute for large groups but gives less detail than the full decomposition.

entries.name: local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of the decomposition that is computed for each individual moment or configuration, instead of averaged over the whole recording. It gives an information time series.

entries.name: neuronal avalanches
entries.background: Cascades of neural firing that spread through a network in bursts of widely varying size. They are often taken as a sign that the brain operates near a critical point.

entries.name: integrated information decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of PID that handles several target variables, so it can split how the past constrains the future into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts.
